system_overview: This specification models PCon, a variant of the classic Paxos consensus algorithm that introduces phase 1c messages to separate the safety-assertion and voting functions of phase 2a messages. In classic Paxos, a phase 2a message both asserts that a value is safe and instructs acceptors to vote for it. In PCon, a phase 1c message asserts safety, and phase 2a is sent only after a corresponding 1c message exists. This variant is useful for reconfiguration scenarios where different sets of acceptors handle different ballots, as the 1c messages propagate safety knowledge and remove dependency on earlier ballot acceptors.
actors_and_components: The system has two types of processes: (1) Acceptors that respond to ballot messages by reporting their vote history (phase 1b) and casting votes (phase 2b). (2) Leaders, one per ballot, that initiate ballots (phase 1a), determine which values are safe (phase 1c), and propose values for voting (phase 2a). Multiple leaders may be active concurrently, and leader selection is not assumed to be reliable.
state_variables: The system tracks four arrays and a message set: (1) For each acceptor, the highest ballot number it has participated in. (2) For each acceptor, the highest ballot number in which it voted (or negative one if never voted). (3) For each acceptor, the value it voted for in its highest voting ballot (or a sentinel if never voted). (4) The set of all messages ever sent, growing monotonically. Messages include five types: 1a (ballot initiation), 1b (acceptor response with vote history), 1c (leader assertion that a value is safe), 2a (leader proposal), and 2b (acceptor vote).
initial_state: All acceptors have maximum ballot negative one, maximum voting ballot negative one, and maximum voting value set to the sentinel. No messages have been sent.
actions: Leader actions: (1) Phase 1a: send a ballot initiation message. (2) Phase 1c: after receiving phase 1b responses from a quorum for a given ballot, determine which values are safe at that ballot (using the ShowsSafeAt predicate that checks quorum responses) and send 1c messages for those values. (3) Phase 2a: if no phase 2a has been sent for this ballot and a 1c message exists for a value at this ballot, send a 2a message proposing that value. Acceptor actions: (4) Phase 1b: if a 1a message exists for a ballot exceeding the acceptor's maximum, update the maximum ballot and respond with current vote history. (5) Phase 2b: if a 2a message exists for a ballot at least equal to the acceptor's maximum, cast a vote for the proposed value, updating all acceptor state accordingly.
safety_properties: Type correctness for all variables and messages. An inductive invariant consisting of five conjuncts: (1) Acceptor state consistency: maximum ballot is at least maximum voting ballot, and the acceptor did not vote in ballots between the two. (2) Phase 1b message accuracy: messages correctly reflect acceptor state at time of sending. (3) Phase 1c correctness: every 1c message asserts a value that is indeed safe at that ballot (per the voting algorithm's safety definition). (4) Phase 2a provenance: every 2a message has a corresponding 1c message. (5) Type correctness. Together these ensure the specification implements the voting algorithm, which in turn implements consensus.
liveness_properties: If there exists a ballot and quorum such that: no higher ballot's phase 1a has been or will be sent, the leader eventually sends a phase 1a for this ballot, each acceptor in the quorum eventually responds to ballot messages, and the leader eventually executes phase 2a if enabled, then eventually some value is chosen.
model_bounds: Constants include the set of choosable values, the set of acceptors, and the set of quorums. Ballots are natural numbers. For model checking, typical values are two values, three acceptors, three quorums of size two, and ballots zero through two.
additional_assumptions: Ballots and acceptors are assumed to be disjoint sets so they can be used as process identifiers simultaneously. The specification uses PlusCal, translated to TLA+. It imports the voting specification and proves refinement: the votes derived from phase 2b messages implement the voting algorithm's vote tracking, and the maximum ballot array directly maps. The ShowsSafeAt predicate checks whether a quorum's phase 1b responses demonstrate safety, potentially using 1c messages from earlier ballots to establish safety of values. Omission faults (message loss, process crashes) are handled implicitly: the safety specification never requires any action to occur.
